task: This is a synthetic exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes as the fixed record: select, organize and phrase the story without inventing additional reported events, scenes, quotations or reporting activity. Write a headline and a reported feature of roughly 450–650 words in AP style for general newspaper readers about the volunteers coordinating short-notice farm-surplus deliveries to small pantries around Fellwater. Write from this reporting snapshot as of September 18, 2026.

facts.text: The fictional Fellwater Produce Link coordinates offers of already harvested surplus from participating farms and deliveries to small community pantries.
The group is a transport and matching operation, not an organization sending volunteers to harvest crops from fields.
Dispatcher Vera Noll begins a delivery day by comparing farm offers with the quantities and delivery times pantries say they can accept.
The supplied scene includes an offer of boxed courgettes and a pantry that can take only part of the load because its storage is nearly full.
Produce that exists at a farm is not automatically a usable donation at every receiving pantry.
Noll said, "The offer arrives as a box count. We still have to find the time, the vehicle and the shelf where those boxes can land."
Volunteer drivers use vehicles agreed through the group's transport arrangements rather than collecting any offered load without coordination.
The group records what was accepted at collection and what each receiving pantry actually took.
Farm grower Elin Marr says surplus offers can change with ordinary sales and harvesting decisions before collection is confirmed.
Marr said, "I can offer what is left when the orders are settled. I cannot turn that into the same donation every Thursday."
The group does not promise pantries a fixed weekly quantity or identical products throughout the season.
A local haulier makes a refrigerated vehicle available on agreed days, but it is not permanently at the volunteers' disposal.
Loads requiring conditions the group cannot provide are declined or referred through another suitable arrangement rather than accepted solely to avoid turning down food.
The recipient pantries remain responsible for their own acceptance and distribution decisions under their operating procedures.
The record describes one coordinated delivery day and provides no annual tonnage or measured reduction in farm waste.
Travel costs are reimbursed from a small community fund; the drivers are volunteers rather than unpaid employees of the farms.
The fund does not pay farmers a market price for donated produce or guarantee to buy unsold crops.
The dispatcher keeps paper contact and route sheets available when a driver cannot receive an electronic update on the road.
A missed collection can affect several recipients, so the group asks farms and pantries to confirm changes before a vehicle is dispatched.
The volunteers hold short end-of-day reviews about practical mismatches, including excess packaging and unsuitable delivery times.
The packet contains no claim about a particular recipient's health or household circumstances.
The group is seeking more regular transport availability, but no additional vehicle commitment has been announced.

forbidden_additions: Volunteer field harvesting, guaranteed weekly quantities or a permanently available refrigerated vehicle.
Annual recovery tonnage, measured waste reduction or recipient health outcomes.
An obligation to buy farms' surplus at market prices.
preserve: The timing and capacity work between an offer and an accepted delivery.
Separate responsibilities of farms, dispatchers, drivers and recipient pantries.
Exact quotation wording and attribution when quotations are used.
